hypotheses.statement: Authority-relevant lowering must preserve and revalidate a context-bound tuple including exact intent identity, basis, selection, closure, revocation, expiry, scope and permit authenticity; otherwise representation changes can silently widen effect authority.
support: E2B C-FFI + JSON IPC 12k cases per boundary
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One or more tuple fields are redundant metadata and can be dropped without changing admissible effect behavior.
hypotheses.falsifier: An ancestry-distinct implementation removes a field while preserving zero false authorizations under targeted stale/reselection/revocation/closure attacks and real capability-object workloads.
hypotheses.next_test: Real WASI/Wasmtime resource/capability handles plus Rust/C/C++ boundary tests.

hypotheses.statement: ClayCode should remain general-purpose by representing destructive/admin/raw operations as typed EffectIntent values while external host capabilities determine whether the current deployment may execute them.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Language-level inexpressibility of destructive operations is necessary for safety and does not materially reduce legitimate general-purpose coverage.
hypotheses.falsifier: A broad systems corpus achieves equivalent legitimate coverage and lower attack surface with destructive/admin/raw effects absent from source semantics, without reintroducing equivalent power through indirect constructs.
hypotheses.next_test: Compile real admin/storage/formatter/embedded corpus under capability profiles and compare expressibility, repair cost and safety.

hypotheses.statement: Selection identity is a first-class causal input to consequential effects and cannot generally be collapsed into basis identity or provenance.
support: selection-check removal: 5000/5000 local, 2500/2500 E2B, and 1000/1000 C-FFI targeted false accepts
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: If basis/provenance and intent are valid, current selection can be reconstructed or omitted safely.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real workloads with adversarial reselection show no behavioral/authority difference when selection binding is removed at matched basis and intent.
hypotheses.next_test: Prompt-injection/retrieval-poisoning corpus that changes selection while holding source records and intent family fixed.

hypotheses.statement: Per-call capability scope is insufficient; cumulative effect admissibility and origin/integrity ancestry require host-side monotone state that cannot be reset or upgraded by model-visible transformations.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Stateless per-call scope/verb checks plus current producer identity are sufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial multi-call and summarization/tool-echo workloads produce no aggregate overshoot or authority laundering under stateless policy.
hypotheses.next_test: Extend Lane-B cross-boundary checker with monotone budget and origin ancestry across IPC/FFI/restart.

hypotheses.statement: Translation validation is the correct promotion boundary for multi-backend ClayCode lowering: compilation success alone is insufficient, but backend-specific bytes/process layout need not share identity if declared semantic/effect behavior is checked.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single canonical implementation/backend is safer and cheaper than repeated translation validation across heterogeneous lowerings.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target benchmarks show translation validation cost/complexity dominates portability benefits without detecting additional semantic faults relative to one verified backend.
hypotheses.next_test: Two independently implemented lowerers over a frozen UECC corpus with mutation-seeded semantic faults.

hypotheses.statement: Destructive physical maintenance such as GC/retention erasure can remain outside model-authored authority while model-side code supplies non-authoritative candidates/hints, preserving general programmability without granting ambient deletion power.
support: 20k synthetic version-DAG trials: protected losses 0 under host-root filtering vs 19854 trials with protected loss under naive model-candidate deletion
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Separating model intent from physical maintenance authority creates unacceptable storage leaks/latency or makes correct retention/erasure impossible.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real storage lifecycle benchmark cannot meet retention/privacy/storage budgets without exposing destructive authority to the model execution profile.
hypotheses.next_test: Nix/OSTree/content-addressed plus database MVCC/GC workload with retention roots and privacy erasure authority.

reason: No formal proof, real WASI capability-object red-team, target-Qwen adherence test, production FRANK trace benchmark, or ancestry-distinct full-stack replication.
